_comment: Config-switched, visual-only material pass for the restock Isaac scene (scripts/twin/restock/visuals.py). The mission RUNTIME config (the Isaac process that composes the stage) reads the top-level 'visuals' key. It is DEFAULT OFF: with the key absent the scene composes byte-identically to today's plain look, so merging this changes nothing until a run opts in. To ENABLE the new look (UR10 palette, neutral-grey mobile base, galvanised-steel rollwagen with a blue plastic base plate, sealed-concrete backroom) add the 'visuals' block below to the run's runtime config. Visual materials ONLY: no geometry, collider, physics, mass, joint, camera, light, QR label, or decode marker is created or changed, so the carton QR and station-camera decode are byte-for-byte unaffected.
_on_off_forms: Enable: "visuals": true  |  "visuals": {"enabled": true}  |  "visuals": "on". Disabled (default): omit the key, or "visuals": false | {"enabled": false} | "off".
_note: UR values follow Universal Robots' own scheme (grey-aluminium housings RAL 9007, light-aluminium link tubes, light-blue joint caps). sRGB hex is converted to linear at author time for the UsdPreviewSurface diffuseColor; the backroom floor/wall re-tone is authored as DIRECT linear (matching the store's own Blender-exported convention) and only overrides the backroom materials in the composed output layer -- the sublayered store file stays read-only. Boot log line: 'VISUALS enabled=.. bound=.. env_retoned=..'.
